1. $f_\theta(x)=W^{(2)}\,\sigma(W^{(1)}x+b^{(1)})+b^{(2)}$ (equivalent notations OK).
2. With a suitable activation and enough hidden units, a one-hidden-layer net can uniformly approximate any continuous function on a compact set to arbitrary accuracy.
3. Size of the net needed; that training will find the parameters; that finite-sample generalization is automatic (any two of these).
4. Deeper compositions can represent some functions more efficiently and learn hierarchical features more easily.
5. Hidden features depend on trainable $\theta$; a kernel $\phi$ is fixed before seeing labels (aside from kernel hyperparameters).
